GOOD TO KNOW

A survey answer of 1 or 2 out of 5 now alerts the agent's team leaders and the floor's supervisors, and books a follow-up call to the customer; an answer of 5 tells the agent and earns them points. Both alerts and the follow-up can be switched off, and what counts as good and bad can be changed, on the Post-call surveys page.

Organisations that use points get the new "Good survey answer" measure (10 points, up to 100 a day) once. Measures an organisation switched off stay off.

Recording file names change only where an organisation sets a format. With no format, downloads and copies are named as before. The file kept on the platform is never renamed.

Download names across the platform may now keep + and ~ characters.

FOR AGENTS

A customer who gives you 5 out of 5 is shown to you with what they wrote, and in My points under what customers said this week. Ten of them earn the Five stars badge.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Customer experience: a new report and page show, per agent, team, queue, campaign or channel, how many answered, the average, and the share of good and bad answers, from the keypad survey during calls, the survey by text after calls, ticket surveys and surveys after written conversations. The page lists the good and bad answers with the customer, the agent, what they wrote and the follow-up. The floor shows today's bad experiences.

A bad answer's alert says who, about which call, conversation or ticket, what the customer wrote, and whether a follow-up call was booked. No follow-up is booked when the customer has no number, asked not to be contacted, or already has one waiting.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Surveys after written conversations: when an agent finishes a web chat, WhatsApp, SMS or email conversation that did not open a ticket, the customer can be asked to rate it from 1 to 5 on the same channel. It is off until you switch it on under Post-call surveys, where you write the question and the thank-you. WhatsApp is asked only within its 24 hours; email sends a link to a short survey page.

Recording file names: under Calls, Recording file names, make formats from parts such as the customer number, start time, call type, call id, agent, campaign, outcome and who hung up, with fixed text, a separator and a date format, and see an example as you go. Every format includes the call id or the recording id so no two recordings get the same name. Mark one as the default, and give a campaign its own in the campaign editor. The name is used when a recording is downloaded and when it is copied by SFTP or FTP; a copy waits for the agent's outcome when the format uses it. A format can be pasted with fixed text written in curly braces, such as {0}."}
